chunks.arabic_text: عُبَيْدُ بْنُ كَثِيرٍ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْوَاحِدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ شَرِيكٍ الْعَامِرِيُّ، الْوَحِيدِيُّ، الْكِلَابِيُّ، أَبُو سَعِيدٍ.

translations.en: ʿUbayd ibn Kathīr ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Sharīk al--ʿĀmirī, al-Waḥīdī, al-Kilābī, Abū Saʿīd.

chunks.arabic_text: كَانَ يُوضَعُ الْحَدِيثَ مُجَاهَرَةً، وَلَا يَحْتَشِمُ الْكَذِبَ الصَّرِيحَ. وَأَمْرُهُ مَشْهُورٌ.

translations.en: He would publicly fabricate ḥadīths and not be shy about his open lying, and his affair is famous.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* characterizes ʿUbayd ibn Kathīr as a narrator who fabricated hadiths openly (*bi-jahāra*), lacking the modesty (*ihtishām*) typically expected of scholars when committing clear falsehoods. His notoriety for this specific trait underscores the critical Shia methodology of scrutinizing narrators' moral integrity (*ʿadāla*) alongside their technical accuracy, as public shamelessness in lying disqualifies one from reliable transmission.
en.seo_question: What is the biographical status of ʿUbayd ibn Kathīr in Shia hadith sciences?
